text:
alex: Heads up — prototyping an 'adaptive-stepper' canary policy for model version upgrades. Goal: start very small, expand faster if signals are clean, but stricter automatic rollback and cooldowns. Posting a config sketch, want quick opinions on thresholds/hold times.

alex: ```yaml
policy: adaptive_stepper
initial_percent: 1
steps: [1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100]
hold_seconds_per_step: [300, 600, 900, 1800, 3600]  # tuneable
max_concurrent_percent: 60
growth_strategy: "time_based"  # other options: metric_confidence, sqrt
rollback_triggers:
  - name: p99_latency_abs
    comparator: ">"
    threshold_ms: 200
    window: 120
  - name: error_rate_rel
    comparator: ">"
    multiplier: 3.0  # 3x relative increase vs baseline
    window: 300
safety_limits:
  min_healthy_replicas: 2
  max_surge_percent_per_minute: 10
  cooldown_on_failure_seconds: 3600
metrics_evaluation_window_seconds: 120
metric_aggregation: "rolling"
```

mira: Quick q — should rollback use p95 or p99? p99 is noisy for small traffic during early steps.

sam: Agree p99 is noisy at 1%. Suggest composite trigger: (p95 > 120ms) OR (p99 > 250ms when traffic >=5%). Also add request success rate relative delta (not only absolute errs).

jordan: UI question — can the console show "predicted time to 100%" based on current hold_seconds + remaining steps? Also need an obvious PAUSE button and reason field persisted for audits.

luisa: For metrics, we need trace sampling + per-route tags so we can attribute spikes to model changes vs infra. Can we tag canary requests with `x-canary-id` and sample at 1% by default?

alex: yep — the plan is deploy-bot emits step events and includes `canary_id`, `step_percent`, `baseline_metrics` snapshot. We'll add `x-canary-id` header so downstream infra/sink can join traces.

deploy-bot: [automated] Canary event: model redwood-md-v2 -> redwood-md-v2.1 started. step=1% canary_id=canary-1839023456

mira: :thumbsup:

sam: Another thought — add an "attenuation" rule: if any trigger fires during hold, reduce next step by factor 0.5 (floor 1%) and extend hold by 2x; if stable for 3 consecutive steps, allow step_size *= 1.5 (cap 50%). This smooths overshoot.

jordan: And add a hard cap: if token-cost per request increases more than 10% consistently, mark as "cost-regression" and pause rollout for product review.

alex: Good call on attenuation + cost-regression. I'll add `attenuate_on_signal` and `cost_regression_threshold` to the schema. Also thinking of adding `grace_period_after_rollforward` to avoid cascading rollouts across clusters.

luisa: Instrumentation checklist: 1) add `x-canary-id` header, 2) emit `canary.step` event to telemetry stream with baseline and delta metrics, 3) attach sample trace ids to event. Without this we can't automagically decide relative deltas.

alex: plan: I'll update the YAML with attenuation, cost check, and p95/p99 hybrid triggers and open PR: http://git/repo/pulls/42 — target review by EOD. anyone object?

sam: fine from runtime side, please include a unit test for selector logic (small-traffic path) and a harness to simulate bursty latency.

jordan: add UI UX affordance for one-click rollback + reason box. Audit log required.

alex: noted. If no other blockers I'll push a v0.1 to `infra-rollout-config` and wire deploy-bot to emit the events for staging canaries.

mira: thanks — this addresses a few product asks for safer upgrades.

alex: merging after PR comments. will follow up with a short demo in tomorrow's standup.
